cells.tense: You are here, and what you settle alone is landing on ground that holds.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Settle something you've already turned over, today, and act on it before explaining it to anyone. The explanation can keep. The move can't.
cells.core:
Some things you turn over alone, and they come out solid. A sense of what deserves attention arrives before your reasons do, and you trust it enough to let it stand without dressing it up. That part is working. It isn't loud. It holds because you don't force it into sentences before it has finished forming, and because you can sit with two sides of something without rushing a verdict to make the room comfortable.

What keeps this honest is the order of operations. Most people explain first and act later, and the explanation ends up steering instead of following. Reverse it once. Take something you've already weighed, settle it before the day is out, and let the doing carry the meaning. The urge to narrate beforehand is where this quietly leaks. Move first, and see whether the decision stands without the preamble.
cells.sheetLine: You've weighed it. Move before you explain.
cells.verb: holding what you know before you say it
cells.place: in the quiet where you decide what deserves your attention

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future that hasn't been written, and the weighing has outrun the week you're in.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Stay with the direction you actually chose, doubt and all, and ask it for no sign that it's working.
cells.core:
You're braced. Something in you has already jumped to how this lands, what it costs, whether the call was right — the whole outcome sketched before the week you're standing in has been lived. The weighing is real, but it has traveled further than the moment it was meant to serve, and all that distance looks like certainty when it isn't. It's the mind finishing a page the pen hasn't reached.

Nothing here asks you to be less sure. Take the direction you genuinely chose — not the safest one, the one — and carry it without demanding evidence that it's working. You already picked it. The stretch ahead is just you holding it. When doubt arrives, let it arrive and don't re-decide. The direction was not the trouble. The trouble was trying to check the ending before the middle was lived.
cells.sheetLine: The ending is written. Come back to the week.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that has already closed, and what used to rise in you stays down.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Use something you already finished, for an hour, and enjoy it instead of improving it. Let it count as done.
cells.core:
The feel for which thing deserves you isn't rising right now. What's here instead is static — the day gets shown up for, the tasks get done, and nothing inside you is pointed anywhere in particular. You aren't empty, and this isn't failure. You're standing on the far side of a door, waiting for something that already came through it, and the waiting has quietly become the whole posture.

What returns this isn't effort. Notice what you already finished and stay with it for one hour — use it, enjoy it, don't reach past it to improve anything. A meal you made and actually eat. A built thing you walk through without touching. What you imagined arriving is already here; the missing piece is the landing. Let one finished thing be finished, and the sense of what deserves you has somewhere to come back to.
cells.sheetLine: Stop reaching past what's already done.

cells.tense: You are weighing two sides quietly, and the pen is down while the page is already in motion.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Accept what's handed back in one exchange — at its real size, neither waved off nor absorbed.
cells.core:
You notice what's fair in this room. Not with a speech — you see it, you move on it, and the place stays calmer because of it. Ask about it and you'd shrug and say you were just paying attention. That shrug is the miss: the discernment is doing real work, and your account of it leaves you out of the frame. A page is being written in a hand you call nothing.

The correction is plain and small. In one exchange this week, let it run both directions — give what you give, and receive what comes back at the size it actually is. Not bigger, not smaller. The reflex is to pass the credit on as easily as you pass everything else, and that reflex keeps the work anonymous. Receiving isn't a favour to the other person. It's how the exchange stays honest, and how you stay inside it.
cells.sheetLine: You see what's fair here. Let some come back.
